thread:
jess: quick dump of today's weird OOMs on prod-rt — attaching profiling notes
jess: observed sudden OOM spikes around 11:23 UTC, ~15 failures in 10m window, all on small-head models (h=16/32)
jess: flame: workspace_alloc() blew up because slot_size computed as roundup(head_dim*kv_slots, slab_gran) => large rounding inflation
jess: hypothesis: FlashAttention kernel path asks for contiguous workspace per head-group which gets multiplied by batch*seq, and small heads trigger coarse slab rounding (slab_gran=256KB) causing 4-5x inflation
liam: can you paste the exact alloc size from the trace?
jess: yep, snippet from runtime trace:
```
AllocRequest(size=1.9M) -> slab_roundup(1.9M) = 2.5M
kv_cache_slots=64, heads=32 => request_per_token ~ 2.5M * 32 = 80M
```
jess: in practice we saw 78-96MB extra per request, which pushed a few hosts across the OOM threshold
oliver: ugh. so small head_dim means smaller base, but slab rounding dominates. we already have slab sizes tuned for throughput; this regresses small models
kate: is this specific to FlashAttention path? or Triton kernels in general?
jess: mostly Flash path because it needs extra workspace for causal fwd/back and typically allocates per-head-group; cuBLASLt path requests smaller continuous workspace but does more temporary tensors elsewhere
liam: could we try a bucketized allocator that uses finer granularity for small allocations? like adaptive bucket sizes: {<32KB:4KB, <256KB:16KB, ...}
oliver: that's similar to jemalloc arenas but we can implement a fast path in our slab allocator: if request < slab_threshold then try sub-slab slotting. avoids global slab roundup
jess: first-pass patch: adaptive_slotting that bisects the slab for requests < 64KB, and tries up to 3 sub-splits before falling back. locally tested: reduced observed inflation from 4.2x -> 1.3x for h=16
kate: any perf penalty for fragmentation? did you simulate long-living KV caches vs ephemeral workspace allocs?
jess: yes — we added a short-lived allocator tag for kernel workspace that gets reclaimed per request; KV caches still use original large aligned slabs. fragmentation was minimal in 30m stress run (alloc churn pattern similar to prod)
liam: telemetry we need: histogram of alloc_request_size, post-roundup_size, slab_roundup_factor per model_id and per-head-dim. then alert when factor>2 for >5% of requests in 5m window
ops-bot: alert rule proposal created: ALLOC_ROUNDUP_FACTOR_HIGH (threshold 2.5) on prod-rt
oliver: fallback plan: if adaptive_slotting triggers >10% fragmentation on a host, mark that host as "slotting_no" in scheduler and route small-head models to cuBLASLt-compatible hosts for 1h
kate: how do we determine cuBLASLt-compatible? we already have kernel compatibility table in runtime metadata
jess: yes, added a quick probe: run microkernel_check on host, ensure cuBLASLt version >= 11.7 and flash-compat flag false
liam: also add a canary rollout: deploy adaptive_slotting on 5% of fleet, collect alloc histograms+OOMs for 1h, then 20% if stable
jess: perf numbers from local bench (h=16, bs=8, seq=1024):
- baseline (no patch): 12.2 ms/op, avg_roundup_factor=4.1
- adaptive_slotting: 12.9 ms/op, avg_roundup_factor=1.3
- cuBLASLt fallback: 13.5 ms/op
so latency regressed ~5% in worst case but memory wins are big
oliver: 5% latency for avoiding OOMs seems fine for prod stability. Can we auto-switch per-model? e.g., model config has prefer_slotting=true/false
kate: yes add model config knob + runtime override per-deployment
jess: open questions:
- how to tune split depth (2 vs 3) for larger slabs
- telemetry tag collisions (we need consistent tag naming: alloc.type=workspace|kv|cache)
- whether to proactively pre-split slabs for models with steady small-head traffic to avoid on-the-fly bisection
liam: for split depth we can adapt: start depth=1, if post-split fragmentation < 0.15 after 5k ops increase depth, else decrease. simple hillclimb
oliver: pre-splitting seems useful for steady-state microservices (embedding-only workloads) but wasteful for bursty traffic; preference: lazy split + background heater for steady models
kate: can you file a runbook for ops if OOM spike recurs during rollout? quick mitigation steps should include: 1) set model routing to cuBLASLt 2) increase host swap_headroom 3) drain non-critical jobs
jess: will draft runbook and PR for telemetry metrics
jess: PR link: https://stash.redwood.internal/p/runtime/patches/1234
liam: I'll own the canary rollout plan and dashboard (alloc hist + oom rate)
oliver: I'll add scheduler flag and host probe
kate: I'll draft the runbook and update model config schema
ops-bot: canary rollout ticket created: RT-4319
jess: thanks all — next steps: PR + canary + 1h observation, aim to merge by EOD if stable :thumbsup:
liam: quick note — add unit test for slab_roundup_factor <= 3 for head_dim<=32 to prevent accidental regressions
jess: adding test now
